_comment: THE WORKED EXAMPLE. Every value here was lifted from the working PAM implementation, not invented:
chain_runner.py lines 68-97 (paths, blocklist, destructive regex, SLA, caps),
generate_flows.py lines 43-85 (context aliases, identity fields, the LOB prelude),
and the measured counts from artifacts/runs/2026-08-05_114315 (OBJ-010).
This file is the proof that the profile schema is sufficient: the PAM harness's entire
project-specific surface fits in it. Read it beside docs/briefs/new-project-implementation.md §8,
which inventories every one of those couplings with its line reference.

project.name: ARCON Privileged Access Management
project.notes: Reference implementation. 122 API modules across 70 controllers.

environment.name: QA_MsSQL
environment.notes: verify_tls false: QA host serves a self-signed certificate. The API port is NOT the app port - environmentUrl is :1302, environmentAPIUrl and pam_BaseAPIURL are :6302. Credentials are committed in plaintext across all 20 env files; treat the file as secret regardless.

roles.note: The only identity available. A second, lower-privilege identity would make authorization testing meaningful; none is provisioned - see unknowns.

auth.notes: lockout_risk is high on measured evidence: repeated /arcontoken calls locked the GenericScheduler service account on 2026-07-28 (ISSUE-009), and that account is also the data-warehouse ETL account, so the blast radius reaches past testing. The lock, not a wrong password, was always the blocker. token_guard.py is the single gate: env var -> valid cache -> ONE live attempt, then latch.

catalogue.count_basis: distinct (controller, action) pairs. The same file also yields 1,336 (all public static String declarations, including header and verb constants), 1,321 (/api/ declarations with duplicates) and 1,308 (distinct path strings). Quote 1,306.
catalogue.notes: No OpenAPI/Swagger exists for this surface. The 37 published Swagger specs (690 operations) describe a DIFFERENT surface with ~6% name overlap. pam/PAM (the product source) implements only 48 of the 1,306 - do not plan on deriving the catalogue from it. /AdminAPI is excluded because it returns 404 on both ports with both credentials.

payloads.notes: 1,289 zero-arg Java methods holding literal request JSON. The literals are stale, which is why only 13 of 217 creates work - the largest single cost in the whole implementation, and still open. A secondary source exists: PAM API (Internal Team).pdf holds 3,194 JSON examples, 1,605-1,654 endpoint-bound depending on basis, but bound BY PAGE PROXIMITY so some bindings are wrong.

envelope.error_code_registry: com.arcon.utils.validation.ErrorCodeRegistry - matches on numeric prefix and records an unrecognised code as an observation. The product has NO published registry; only 3 codes are documented anywhere.
envelope.notes: status_is_authoritative false is measured, not assumed: 1,022 of 5,416 cases (18.9%) returned HTTP 200 while failing validation. 31 shapes were counted across 1,868 retained bodies, of which only 6 match a documented one; 127 responses were not JSON objects at all, 288 carried no Success field, 139 of 1,291 Result values were not arrays, and 2 bodies were a naked true/false. Success:true is NOT evidence of a write - SetServiceDetails answers Success:true with Message 'Already Exists' when nothing was inserted. Casing matters: PascalCase Success appears 1,580 times, camelCase success 0 times.

identity_prelude.name: GetLOBList
identity_prelude.note: Selected BY NAME so the id is discovered rather than hardcoded. Result[0] is LOB 1 (O11), which has no user groups - blind first-row chaining fails here.

identity_prelude.name: GetUserGroupList
identity_prelude.note: A real join: this endpoint exposes LOBName, not LobId, so the NAME carried from hop 1 is the join key.

blocklist.GetLogs: hangs 30 s and stops the IIS application pool (ISSUE-010)
blocklist.GetErrorLogs: hangs 30 s and stops the IIS application pool (ISSUE-010)
blocklist.GetAllActiveUserDetails: hung 30 s on every version during the GET run

safety.notes: The blocklist is enforced at planning time, before a request is built - three sequential calls to GetLogs took the entire API to 503 with no recovery, and that was not a load test. Name-based guarding is mandatory here because deletion is expressed as POST /api/<Controller>/Delete<Thing>: a destructive call is indistinguishable from an ordinary POST by verb. Teardown disabled leaves 146 destructive rows unexecuted and this run's created records in place - stated, not hidden. body_cap exists because one endpoint returns 1.1 MB with no filter parameter.

validation.notes: The Python harness asserts L1-L7. L8-L12 (schema, mandatory-fields, business-rule, db-persistence, security) exist in the Java framework as com.arcon.utils.validation and are not wired into the harness. Keep L3 and L4: status_is_authoritative is false, so dropping them leaves nothing that can detect a rejected request. sla_ms is split because writes take 5-7 s here and a single read-tuned budget fails every write.

reporting.notes: Retaining every run is what made the N-1 vs N benchmark possible, and what let a corrected validator re-score 1,868 baseline hops offline with zero HTTP calls.
